gaps.title: D53, from-log path: sets after a re-establishment of a pending or unlogged exercise come back two at once
gaps.detail: D53 (R6-LOAD-ESTABLISHMENT, shared with R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION and R6-ROTATION; found in round 11; fixed in round 12 for a known-load state only) r6-program.mjs advanceStrength: the regain cap (regainCap) is set only in the branch that converts a known-load state (reestablishes(ex,u) requires ex.mode === 'KNOWN'). strengthDose prescribes the same "Not done for more than 28 days" row for a from-log state, that is an exercise whose establishment log is still pending confirmation or that was performed without a usable log, and that re-establishment starts no regain, so a block-boundary set comes back at once. Probe AI, noisy-log grid (192 timelines in which the establishment logs of exercises without a known dose alternate 20 and 40 kg, so they stay pending as D45 intends): 592 of 1,224 performed re-establishments start from a from-log state, and 48 next exposures exceed the allowance: 24 are prescribed two sets above the re-establishment (2 -> 4 sets at RIR 3) and 24 fall in a consolidation week whose count before the reduction is two above. Probe AJ reproduces it with consistent logs after the gap: a goblet squat and a dumbbell RDL whose establishment log stayed pending through the block that ended in week 4 are re-established at 2 sets in week 10 and prescribed 4x5 in week 11, also when the re-establishment log is adopted (4x10). On the known-load path the fix holds (0 of 2,448 in the as-prescribed grid). This still contradicts strength.setsAfterReestablishment ("its earlier set count comes back one set per executed week, never at once") and conditions LE-15, PP-14 and ROT-10. Required change (runtime only): start the regain at every performed re-establishment by effort after more than return.moderateMaxDays (every performed "Not done for more than" exposure), whatever the state's mode (known load, pending establishment log, unlogged, re-established); the prescribed count, including any block-boundary set, then rises at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, from the re-establishment count up to the count the exercise would otherwise have, with phase reductions on top. Regression tests: a pending establishment log with a block-boundary set earned before the gap, one whose block credit is earned by the re-establishment week, an unlogged state and the adopted variant (probes AJ and the noisy-log grid of AI).
gaps.owner: ENGINEERING (R7 runtime author) with the SSCTR

gaps.title: D54: a re-establishment row ignores the taper, race-week and post-event strength doses
gaps.detail: D54 (R6-EVENT-TRANSITION and R6-LOAD-ESTABLISHMENT; found in round 12; the row predates FREEZE-1 and became reachable in ordinary use with the D52 (B) fix) r6-program.mjs strengthDose: the re-establishment row of an exercise not performed for more than return.moderateMaxDays (min(goal sets, 2) sets at RIR >= 3, effort-guided under the earlier load) is returned before the phase reduction is computed, so it ignores the taper, race-week and post-event doses, while the first-establishment and "No usable load" rows take the reduced count. Probe AK (10K and half marathon in week 13 of 16; goals STRENGTH, RUNNING_SUPPORT and GENERAL; strength missed in the five weeks before each phase; compared with a twin executed throughout) finds 70 re-establishment rows above the phase dose of the same exercise on the same date: 18 in race week, 6 days before the race (main lifts at 2 sets at RIR 3 against 1 set at RIR >= 4), 24 in the post-event week, 4 days after it (2 sets at RIR 3 against one light session of 1 set at RIR >= 4), and 28 in the taper week (2 sets against 1). None in consolidation or specific weeks, where the re-establishment count is at or below the reduced count. This contradicts policy principle 8 (strength stays at a reduced dose across event phases), operational.event (raceWeekStrengthSets 1 at raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir 4, postEventStrengthSets 1, taperStrengthSetFraction 0.5) and R6-EVENT-TRANSITION conditions 7 and 8. Required change (runtime only): a re-establishment row takes the phase reduction like the other establishment rows: never more sets than the phase dose the exercise would otherwise have that day and never fewer reps in reserve than the phase minimum; the load stays effort-guided under the earlier ceiling. Regression tests: a re-establishment due in a taper, race-window and post-event session for a 3-set and a 2-set goal (probe AK).
